title: What If a Plague Broke Out Inside a Video Game? In 2005 One Did

scenes.text: What if a plague broke out inside a video game? In 2005 one did. Scientists took notes.
In World of Warcraft, a boss monster cast a spell called Corrupted Blood. It was meant to stay inside one dungeon.
But infected players teleported to the cities, and their pets carried it too. Soon the streets were littered with skeletons.
The makers tried a quarantine. Players ignored it. Healers rushed in and spread it further. A few infected others on purpose.
After about a week, the company gave up and rebooted the game.
Two epidemiologists wrote it up in a medical journal: real people don't behave like the models. In 2020, the world saw why.

description:
What if a plague broke out inside a video game?
In 2005 one did. In World of Warcraft, the boss Hakkar in the Zul'Gurub raid cast a damaging, contagious spell called Corrupted Blood that was meant to stay in that dungeon. Infected players teleported out, and a glitch let pets and computer-controlled characters carry it into the cities, where low-level characters died almost at once. Around four million characters were affected. A quarantine failed because players ignored it; healers trying to help kept the infection going, the curious came to watch, and some players spread it deliberately. After about a week the publisher, Blizzard, reset the servers. Epidemiologists Eric Lofgren and Nina Fefferman analysed the outbreak in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2007, arguing that it showed human behaviour that mathematical models leave out; the paper was widely revisited during COVID-19.

first_comment: Players with pets got blamed for spreading it. What would you have done: heal, run, or go and look?
